lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Circles, Angles, Area, and Surface Area
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: unknown angles

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: Two angles are supplementary. Their measures are (4x + 6)° and (2x + 24)°. Find the value of x and the measure of each angle.

steps: Combine like terms: 6x + 30 = 180, so 6x = 150 and x = 25.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: Three angles lie along a straight line and measure 65°, 49°, 40°, and x°. What is the value of x?
A figure is a 10-by-13 rectangle topped by a triangle. The triangle's base equals the rectangle's width, 10 units, and its height is 5 units. What is the total area of the figure, in square units?
A rectangle has an area of 72 square units and a width of 5 units. What is its exact length, in units?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A rectangular prism has length 8, width 13, and height 10 (all in units). What is its exact surface area, in square units?
What is the exact volume of a rectangular prism with length 9, width 10, and height 7 (units)? Give your answer in cubic units.
A circle has a radius of 9 in. What is its exact circumference? Express your answer as a multiple of π.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: A circle has a circumference of 17π cm. What is its exact radius?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A circle has a radius of 3 m. What is its exact area? Express your answer as a multiple of π (use a fraction for the coefficient if it is not a whole number).
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
